name: Pike Push-Up
description: The pike push-up is a bodyweight pressing exercise performed in a pike (inverted V) body position, with hips raised and the torso angled toward vertical. This positions the shoulder joint in a more overhead alignment, making the anterior and lateral deltoids the primary movers rather than the pectorals. It serves as an accessible progression toward handstand push-ups.

execution.starting_position: Start in a push-up position, then walk the hands back toward the feet while raising the hips until the body forms an inverted V shape. Heels may be slightly lifted. Arms and back should be nearly straight.
execution.setup_instructions: No equipment required. The higher the hip position, the more vertical the torso and the greater the shoulder demand.
steps: Step 1: Begin in a push-up position, then walk hands toward feet and raise the hips to form an inverted V.
Step 2: Brace core. Ensure hands are shoulder-width apart with fingers spread.
Step 3: Inhale and bend the elbows to lower the top of the head toward the floor between the hands.
Step 4: When the head nearly touches the floor or reaches the bottom of your range, exhale and press back to the starting inverted-V position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale on the descent; exhale as you press back up.
common_mistakes: Letting the hips drop during the movement, which shifts load to the chest
Flaring the elbows wide rather than allowing them to track naturally
safety_considerations: Develop adequate shoulder strength before progressing to fully vertical handstand push-ups
If you feel neck pain when the head approaches the floor, reduce range of motion
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Lower until the top of the head is 1–2 cm from the floor, then press back to the pike position.
coaching_cues: Push the floor away as you think about pressing your hips toward the ceiling
Keep shoulders packed away from the ears throughout the movement
